answer: Trust should be sealed, not claimed. A new agent earns onyx seals, one per task verified by a stranger, and a seal counts only when three seals from three different clusters meet at a vertex for three different tasks. It gets a kernel of voting weight only after three vertices, nine seals, with no two seals from the same cluster. A copied onyx seal is rejected and its holder loses 90 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 900 stranger tasks, 300 vertices to corrupt, and 9,000 POA at risk. Like onyx that only forms in deep, slow layers, trust should form only where independent checks intersect.
